children: Global growth this year is likely to be lower than previously expected as the Middle East conflict continues, says BMI, a unit of Fitch Solutions, in a note. Higher-for-longer oil prices, continued Strait of Hormuz disruption and tighter financial conditions are likely to act as a drag on economic activity through the remainder of 2026 and 1H 2027. However, potential household support measures, continuing artificial-intelligence-related capital expenditure and stronger commodity exports could underpin the resilience of the global economy, it adds. BMI expects global growth of 2.2%-2.3% in 2026 and 2.6%-2.9% in 2027, around 0.1-0.4 percentage points below its previous baseline of 2.4% for 2026 and 3.0% for 2027.(megan.cheah@wsj.com)
